Every one was shaped with HarfBuzz in the original and the patched font of its style. The original reproduces the mark position printed in the PDF except in 1 combo, marked †, all in semibold: the PDF was set with another release of that font, so its ``original'' column is 7.051, not what the book printed. 
A combo is listed if a mark is not anchored in the original or the patched font (it is then drawn where its outline lies, after the base's advance) or the patch moves a mark by at least 10 units. In each style, combos anchored in neither font come first: those the patch does not fix.
Each is shown in the first word of the PDF that has it, without the punctuation around it, every character in the style the PDF set it in, super- and subscripts as printed. Page = the book's printed page number, as part:page (1:93), since the parts' paginations overlap (the back matter of part~1 has the numbers of the first chapters of part~2).
Line = the text line on that page, counted from the top without the running header; every text line counts, including table rows, gloss lines and footnotes.
Columns: original, patched, and the two overlaid (patched in \textcolor{patchred}{red} over the original in black; only marks that move show red). Move = patched minus original mark position, (x, y) in font units, per mark.

\subsection*{p.~1:93}A mark cited on its own after a space (“marked in the transcription by the diacritic ̭”). In the PDF the mark sits in the space, much as in the NBSP row, so this is not a visible problem; but U+0020 has no anchors in either font, and only an anchored base guarantees the placement: the patch gives NBSP x-height anchors for floating marks (U+25CC dotted circle is the other usual base).\par\smallskip

\subsection*{Checked in context: not font problems}p.~1:143, example (16), \emph{*̆ḷə ḡawwāyā} `inside': an encoding typo. The PDF has a stray U+0306 after the asterisk (the starred-form marker); the word begins with ḷ, which should not also carry a breve. In print the breve falls on the asterisk and is nearly invisible, but it is in the text. p.~1:65, (10), \emph{zīyāy, zīyā}: mutool reports the U+0304 of ī in the subset of LibertinusSerif-Regular after an italic i, but the zero-width mark's own outline lands over the i and hides its dot, so it looks right; the bold letters are deliberate. Not a font issue. p.~2:708, (77b), \emph{lā́̀} `cop' (italic, listed under Other combos): ā with both an acute and a grave, the only such stack in the book; (76b) on the same page has \emph{lā̀} `cop', so the acute is probably stray. The patch stacks both marks on the macron, so it prints as typed.\par\medskip
